flavor.scarlet: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.
flavor.violet: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.

flavor.scarlet: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.
flavor.violet: It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.

flavor.scarlet: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.
flavor.violet: It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.

flavor.scarlet: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.
flavor.violet: It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.

flavor.scarlet: This mysterious Pokémon has some similarities to a creature that an old book introduced as Slither Wing.
flavor.violet: This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.

flavor.scarlet: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.
flavor.violet: It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine.

flavor.scarlet: This Pokémon closely resembles a scientific weapon that a paranormal magazine claimed was sent to this planet by aliens.
flavor.violet: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

flavor.scarlet: Its shape is similar to a robot featured in a paranormal magazine article. The robot was said to have been created by an ancient civilization.
flavor.violet: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

flavor.scarlet: It is very similar to a cyborg covered exclusively by a paranormal magazine. The cyborg was said to be the modified form of a certain athlete.
flavor.violet: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

flavor.scarlet: It resembles a certain Pokémon introduced in a paranormal magazine, described as the offspring of a Hydreigon that fell in love with a robot.
flavor.violet: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

flavor.scarlet: This Pokémon resembles an unknown object described in a paranormal magazine as a UFO sent to observe humanity.
flavor.violet: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.

flavor.scarlet: It has some similarities to a Pokémon introduced in a dubious magazine as a Tyranitar from one billion years into the future.
flavor.violet: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

flavor.scarlet: Frigibax absorbs heat through its dorsal fin and converts the heat into ice energy. The higher the temperature, the more energy Frigibax stores.
flavor.violet: This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.

flavor.scarlet: Arctibax freezes the air around it, protecting its face with an ice mask and turning its dorsal fin into a blade of ice.
flavor.violet: It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.

flavor.scarlet: This Pokémon blasts cryogenic air out from its mouth. This air can instantly freeze even liquid-hot lava.
flavor.violet: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.

flavor.scarlet: The grudge of a person punished for writing the king’s evil deeds upon wooden tablets has clad itself in dead leaves to become a Pokémon.
flavor.violet: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.

flavor.scarlet: This Pokémon can control 100 tons of fallen snow. It plays around innocently by leaping in and out of avalanches it has caused.
flavor.violet: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.

flavor.scarlet: The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.
flavor.violet: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

flavor.scarlet: It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.
flavor.violet: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

flavor.scarlet: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.
flavor.violet: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.

flavor.scarlet: It has some similarities to a mad scientist’s invention covered in a paranormal magazine.
flavor.violet: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

flavor.scarlet: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.
flavor.violet: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.

flavor.scarlet: Much remains unknown about this creature. It resembles Cyclizar, but it is far more ruthless and powerful.
flavor.violet: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

flavor.scarlet: This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.
flavor.violet: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.

flavor.scarlet: Many of its physical characteristics match those of a Virizion from the future that was covered in a paranormal magazine.
flavor.violet: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

flavor.scarlet: After all its muscles were stimulated by the toxic chain around its neck, Okidogi transformed and gained a powerful physique.
flavor.violet: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

flavor.scarlet: The chain is made from toxins that enhance capabilities. It stimulated Munkidori's brain and caused the Pokémon's psychic powers to bloom.
flavor.violet: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.

flavor.scarlet: Fezandipiti owes its beautiful looks and lovely voice to the toxic stimulants emanating from the chain wrapped around its body.
flavor.violet: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.

flavor.scarlet: This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.
flavor.violet: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

flavor.violet: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

flavor.violet: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

flavor.violet: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

flavor.scarlet: There are scant few reports of this creature being sighted. One short video shows it rampaging and spouting pillars of flame.
flavor.violet: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.

flavor.scarlet: It's said to incinerate everything around it with lightning launched from its fur. Very little is known about this creature.
flavor.violet: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.

flavor.scarlet: It resembles a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a Terrakion that had been modified by an evil organization.
flavor.violet: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.

flavor.scarlet: It resembles a mysterious object introduced in a paranormal magazine as a cutting-edge weapon shaped like a Cobalion.
flavor.violet: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.

flavor.scarlet: Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.
flavor.violet: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.

flavor.scarlet: It feeds others toxic mochi that draw out desires and capabilities. Those who eat the mochi fall under Pecharunt’s control, chained to its will.
flavor.violet: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.
